items.title: 68728_Jonah
items.q: And Bern Back was a big man, official, in the national union, not 802, in the national.

ctx.x: Walk the streets and stuff. So then we said, well, we're going back to New York. We told Red Colonna, who was Jerry Colonna's brother, he owned the place, he and a guy named Parker, they owned the Famous Door, and so we told them we were going to put in a notice. We'd been there about two months and a half. We were going to put in a notice. He said, "You can't put in no notice. We have a contract on you with Consolidated Radio Artists that you have to stay here six months. We can't fire you and you can't quit."…

So, Saturday come and so they called up -- somebody calls up from New York, long distance on the phone, and says, "We want to speak to Stuff Smith." So Stuff says okay, so he answered the phone. So he come back to the bandstand and I said who was that. He said some guy said he was Bern Back. And Bern Back was a big man, official, in the national union, not 802, in the national. Bern Back was his name. So he said it was some guy said it was Bern Back, said not to leave. He said, "Stay on your job." So we said we…

So that morning, we got on the train and we come on back home. And we laid around awhile. So Joe Helbarth had been telling us come on back, because they wasn't doing too good in there, you know. Business was bad, because Kirby hadn't got the band set. In fact I don't know if it was Kirby's band or not, because they had Leo Watson they were trying to take out of the Spirits of Rhythm. They took Leo out of there, and they had Pete Brown. They had Frankie Newton and some other guys. So maybe he had -- yeah, he did,…
